findings.observed: 200 for both the wellness-instructor token and the devotee token. Body: {"online":false,"mode":{"chat":true,"call":true}}. The handler at apps/api/src/routes/astrologer-portal.ts:398 is the only route in that file with no ASTROLOGER role check — /dashboard (:160), /profile (:282), /availability (:327), POST /online (:375) and /earnings (:409) all guard with roles.includes('ASTROLOGER'), and all five correctly returned 403 for the same two tokens. I am deliberately NOT rating this P0 despite the brief's default rule for a 200 on a wrong-role /astrologer-portal/* route, because the body contains no other user's data: getAstrologerPresence is keyed on request.currentUser.id, so a non-astrologer only ever reads their own always-default presence and no astrologer's real status is reachable through it. It is a missing guard, not a cross-tenant read. The write path is correctly closed (POST /online with the wellness token returns 403), so a non-astrologer cannot make themselves appear in the live directory.

findings.observed: Both return 500 {"error":"InternalServerError","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"} with the generic Hindi user-facing message. The handler uses a bare z.object({online: z.boolean(), chat: ..., call: ...}).parse(request.body ?? {}) at apps/api/src/routes/astrologer-portal.ts:381-387; .parse throws a ZodError that nothing catches, so client input error surfaces as a server fault. Two consequences: the caller is told the server broke when in fact their request was malformed, and every malformed toggle logs as a 5xx, which will poison error-rate alerting on the endpoint an astrologer hits most often. The sibling route GET /wellness-portal/instructor/mine already does this correctly (safeParse then 400 with issues), so the right pattern exists in the codebase.

repro: Scroll to 'Weekly Schedule' and click any orange 'Book' button next to a class
findings.observed: Nothing happens. The Book buttons in the weekly schedule are bare <button> elements with no onClick, no form, no wrapping Link and no href — and both pages are server components (neither file carries a 'use client' directive), so no handler can be attached at runtime. They are structurally inert. apps/web/app/wellness/yoga/page.tsx has two of them (line 274 in the morning block, line 311 in the evening block) and apps/web/app/wellness/meditation/page.tsx one (line 396), rendering roughly ten dead Book buttons across the two pages. Each sits directly beneath a scarcity line such as '4 spots left', which is the strongest possible prompt to click. The pages' other CTA, 'Book a Session' at yoga/page.tsx:376, is a real Link but points at /wellness — the hub the visitor just came from, not a booking flow. So the flagship yoga and meditation landing pages offer no working path to enrol in anything.

blocked.target: /astrologer-portal/* and /wellness-portal/* page bodies as a signed-in provider
blocked.reason: Cannot establish a browser session without /auth/login, which the brief forbids. In production the auth context deliberately does NOT persist the access token to localStorage (apps/web/lib/auth-context.tsx:465 removes poojly_session outside the compile-time-dead demo branch), and the API's darshya_session cookie is host-only for api.darshya.online so it cannot be replayed against darshya.online (documented in apps/web/middleware.ts:79-90). A cached bearer token therefore cannot be injected into the page's auth state. Mitigation: the full data layer was proved instead — every portal API these pages call returns 200 with a correct empty shape for its own role and 401/403 otherwise — and all 15 page shells were confirmed to render server-side without an error boundary. What remains unverified is only the client-side rendering of those empty shapes.
